did_you_know.text: Did you know? In chapter 2, verse 5, God addresses Ezekiel as “son of man” and commands him to stand on his feet before speaking to him.
Did you know? Ezekiel describes how the Spirit entered him, set him on his feet, and then he heard the one speaking to him.
Did you know? Ezekiel’s mission is to the Israelites, who are described in the chapter as “rebellious nations” against the Lord; the text emphasizes that their ancestors also rebelled against him.
Did you know? The people are described as “stubborn and hardhearted,” and Ezekiel is commanded to speak God’s word to them despite their resistance.
Did you know? The success of Ezekiel’s mission does not depend on whether the people listen: whether they listen or refuse, they will know that a prophet has been among them.
Did you know? To strengthen Ezekiel, the Lord warns him not to be afraid of the people’s words or their looks, and describes his opponents as “briers and thorns” and “scorpions.”
Did you know? Ezekiel is commanded to speak God’s words to the people in every situation, whether they listen or refuse, because they are again defined as “a rebellious house.”

Did you know? Ezekiel is commanded not to be rebellious himself, but to open his mouth and eat what the Lord gives him; this command emphasizes that the prophet must receive the message before delivering it.
Did you know? In his vision, Ezekiel sees a hand stretched out toward him, holding a scroll, which is presented to him in preparation for his mission.
Did you know? The scroll is written on both sides, and on it are written “lamentations, mourning, and woe”—expressions describing grief, sighing, and sorrow.
